title: A massive dense gas cloud close to the nucleus of the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068
question: What is the nature of the 689 GHz continuum peak close to the nucleus S1 of NGC 1068, and what role does it play in nuclear star formation and gas inflow?

what.value: S1 nuclear position from 8.4 GHz VLBA/VLA astrometry

evidence.quote: The position of S1 reported in (cite: G04) was obtained through astrometry between the 8.4 GHz continuum image taken by VLBA

evidence.loc: 5.2 Origin of the Massive Dense Gas Cloud

what.value: Stellar population ages 300 Myr and 30 Myr

evidence.quote: one is the relatively young stellar population with an age of 300 Myr

recipe.method: Set rest frequency, rebin velocity by 2 channels, export to FITS, import into GILDAS, shift origin to S1

recipe.goal: Measure continuum peak and moment maps
recipe.method: Peak intensity and flux in beam; moments over 1020-1240 km/s

recipe.goal: Dust SED gas mass, Lbol, SFR
recipe.method: Single-temperature grey body fit of 689 GHz flux; Lbol from optically thin dust; SFR from Kennicutt 1998
key_parameters: Td 50-70 K, beta=1.7, kappa0=0.005 cm/g at 231 GHz

recipe.goal: Estimate cloud size via RADEX beam filling and peak positions
recipe.method: RADEX non-LTE with CO/H2~1e-4, Tgas=Td, FWHM 30 km/s; Tsb/TR gives filling factor and size; compared to peak-pixel scatter
Mvir from Reff and sigma_3D; M* = eps*Mgas with SFE a few-10%

evidence.quote: the angular separation corresponds to the projected separation of $\simeq$ 14 pc
we calculated SFR to be $\sim$ 0.1 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$
optical depth of the line of $\tau_\mathrm{\tiny CO6-5}\sim 15$
Repeating the same analysis for the red, we obtained $2r\sim 8$ pc.

not_stated_but_needed: Image pixel size and beam parameters (blank in text)
Exact aperture/beam geometry and peak-pixel fitting procedure
Details of RADEX inputs beyond those given
score_reason: Public image products and clear recipe with simple formulae, but some parameters missing and results are order-of-magnitude.
rediscovery_reason: Public image products and numeric results derivable from stated assumptions.
